**Indikator 13** is a clinical quality indicator in the Danish healthcare system that measures the proportion of newly diagnosed patients with [[atrieflimren]] who die within one year of their diagnosis [^src1]. It serves as a central quality objective for evaluating survival and recovery outcomes in cardiovascular care [^src1]. The indicator is featured in the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database's annual report, published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP), which systematically monitors clinical performance alongside other metrics like severe bleeding (Indikator 12) [^src1]. 

During the measurement period of July 1, 2021, to June 30, 2022, the national one-year mortality rate for newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients in [[danmark|Danmark]] was 13.1% (95% CI: 12.6–13.5) [^src1]. The report also breaks down these outcomes at the institutional level to enable local performance comparisons. At [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]], the one-year mortality rate for this cohort was notably higher at 21.3% (95% CI: 15.6–28.0) [^src1]. In contrast, [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] reported a rate of 16.4% (95% CI: 14.1–18.9) [^src1]. By tracking these figures, Indikator 13 provides essential data for clinical improvement initiatives and policy-making regarding atrial fibrillation treatment across different regions and hospitals [^src1].
